title: Request Gatekeeper: latency-aware priority gating with kernel-feedback
creator: Claire Zhang
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime-level admission controller ("Request Gatekeeper") that gates incoming prefill and decode requests using latency SLO awareness, kernel-selection feedback (current kernel hot/cold state and estimated kernel occupancy), and per-tenant fairness counters. The Gatekeeper should reduce tail latency regressions under load while preserving reasonable throughput and bounded cost.

Motivation: Current schedulers make decisions primarily at phase split and token granularity but are relatively blind to the real-time state of the selected execution kernels. When a chosen kernel becomes saturated or cold (cross-block data movement, memory pressure, or quantized-kernel inefficiencies), some requests suffer large latency spikes. Additionally, tenants with bursty traffic can starve latency-sensitive small requests. We need a prefill/decode admission policy that blends: 1) kernel feedback signals, 2) tenant fairness/deficit accounting, and 3) latency SLO objectives to decide whether to admit, queue, or redirect (fallback) requests.

Scope: Admission controller in the serving runtime; lightweight state per-GPU and per-tenant; integration points: kernel-selection telemetry, allocator, and routing fallback layer. Does NOT include new model quantization kernels or major kernel changes -- consumes kernel signals exposed by kernel infra work.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper component built and compiled within runtime, behind feature flag
Admission decisions use kernel-state signal (hot/cold/occupancy estimate) + tenant deficit counters

Under synthetic mixed workload (latency-sensitive small prompts + throughput batch jobs), 95th-token latency for latency-sensitive cohort improves >= 20% vs baseline without Gatekeeper, while overall throughput reduction <= 8%
Unit and integration tests covering decision logic edge cases (kernel unavailable, tenant unregistered, failing metrics), and a canary rollout plan
Run A/B experiment for 2 weeks on small percent of production traffic with rollout dashboard and automated rollback trigger
design_notes:
High-level algorithm: Maintain per-GPU kernel occupancy estimate (sliding window of recent kernel active cycles and dispatch queue length) and a kernel temperature flag (hot/cold) derived from probe latency and cache miss indicators. Maintain per-tenant deficit counters that decay over time. For each incoming request: 1) compute request profile (prefill estimated tokens, decode budget, latency sensitivity label from token_limit or client hint); 2) compute admission_score = w1 * latency_sensitivity_score + w2 * (1 - normalized_kernel_occupancy) + w3 * tenant_deficit_factor; 3) if admission_score >= admit_threshold -> admit; else if admission_score >= queue_threshold -> enqueue on short queue with priority; else -> redirect to fallback model variant or respond with rate-limit. 

Key heuristics: 
- Weighting: default weights initially w1=0.5, w2=0.3, w3=0.2; expose as runtime flags for tuning.
- Kernel feedback: kernel_occupancy normalized to [0,1]; kernel_temperature transitions guarded by hysteresis to avoid flapping.
- Fairness: tenant_deficit increases on accepts proportional to estimated token cost and decays at configurable rate; deficit reduces chance of acceptance for heavy tenants until decay recovers.
- Phase awareness: use prefill vs decode phase annotations to prefer admitting prefill-heavy requests ahead of long decode phases if decode kernel occupancy is high.

Implementation components: 
- Admission controller module (Go/Rust): decision API used by front-end request handler before enqueuing into prefill/decode allocator.
- Kernel signal exporter: small shim in kernel selection layer that exposes occupancy and temperature via in-memory ring buffer (read-only) to avoid RPC.
- Short-queue with eviction policy: per-GPU bounded queue (N=32) for queued small requests with LIFO for latency-sensitive requests.
- Telemetry: Prometheus metrics + Event logs for gate decisions; traces for queued request path.
- Feature flags and rollout controls in console for per-customer enablement.
implementation_plan:
Week 1: API skeleton + kernel signal shim + unit tests. Week 2: integrate admission logic and tenant-deficit bookkeeping; end-to-end local simulation harness. Week 3: add telemetry + Prometheus metrics + integrate with allocator queue. Week 4: internal dogfood on staging, run stress tests and tune weights. Week 5: canary 1% production, monitor for 48h and iterate. Week 6: expand canary and finalize docs.

PRs and work items: Create runtime PR for admission component; small change in kernel-selection to emit occupancy; change in front-end handler to call Gatekeeper.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10 - Ticket created by Claire Zhang. Initial proposal and tradeoffs documented.

2025-02-13 - Spike: implemented a simple kernel occupancy estimator in the kernel-selection shim; synthetic microbench shows occupancy correlates with observed dispatch latency (R=0.78). Saved as experimental metric in staging.

2025-02-18 - Implemented tenant deficit counter prototype and a simple admission_score. Ran local simulator with mixed workload; initial tuning achieved 18% 95th reduction for latency cohort but throughput dropped ~12% (we need to tighten thresholds).

2025-02-22 - Design review with PM and runtime owners. Action items: add hysteresis to kernel_temperature, add short-queue eviction LIFO for latency-sensitive requests, and expose admission weights as runtime knobs. Assigned Miguel for integration work.
2025-02-27 - Implemented hysteresis and LIFO queue; unit tests added. Bench harness updated to model fallback redirect to smaller model variant (gpt-lite) reducing latency for denied requests.

2025-03-03 - Internal staging run with mixed tenants (10 tenants): observed 95th latency improvement of 22% and throughput drop reduced to 6.5% after tuning. Captured metrics dashboard and initial PR (#4387) opened. Requesting review from runtime infra: @Asha Patel and @Owen Brooks.
2025-03-04 - Quick follow-up: added an opt-out label for enterprise tenants that require strict throughput SLAs; also prepared canary rollout plan and rollback criteria.
review_feedback: Asha Patel (runtime infra): ensure occupancy estimator is lock-free and cannot be gamed by adversarial clients; add upper bound on estimator influence.
Owen Brooks (SRE): add detailed SLO-based automated rollback triggers (if p99 increases > 10% for control group).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: unfairly throttling large but latency-tolerant tenants causing billing complaints. Mitigation: per-tenant opt-out and explicit fallback to a cheaper model variant or reserved capacity routing.
Risk: kernel signal noise causing flapping admission decisions. Mitigation: hysteresis, smoothing window, and upper/lower clamps on occupancy influence.
Risk: complexity in debugging admission decisions. Mitigation: emit structured event logs with decision factors for each gated request and add a debug endpoint that replays decision inputs.
Risk: additional CPU overhead in front-end path. Mitigation: keep estimator updates lock-free and decision logic O(1) with precomputed thresholds; measured < 2% CPU overhead in staging.
rollout_plan:
Start behind feature flag. Canary 1% traffic for 72h, monitor p50/p95/p99 for latency-sensitive cohorts, overall throughput, and gate metric ratios. If any of: p99 regresses > 10% for any tenant, gate drop rate > 5% and sustained for 15m, or errors in decision path increase, rollback flag. After stable canary, ramp to 10% for 48h then 50% for 48h then full rollout. Provide per-customer enable toggle in Console.

Post-rollout: run 2-week experiment comparing cost per 1M tokens and tail latency improvements and collect customer qualitative feedback.
